metadata.created_for: LLM comparison evaluation across codellama:latest, qwen2.5:0.5b, tinyllama:1.1b
metadata.instructions: Send IDENTICAL questions to all three models. Do not change questions, retrieval, prompts, or embeddings between runs.

questions.question: What is the Central Goods and Services Tax (CGST) Act?
questions.ground_truth: The Central Goods and Services Tax Act, 2017 (Act No. 12 of 2017) is an Act enacted by the Parliament of India to make a provision for levy and collection of tax on intra-State supply of goods or services or both by the Central Government.
questions.notes: Straightforward factual question answered directly from the opening of cgst_act.pdf.

questions.question: What is the meaning of 'aggregate turnover' under the CGST Act?
questions.ground_truth: Aggregate turnover means the aggregate value of all taxable supplies (excluding inward supplies on which tax is payable on reverse charge basis), exempt supplies, exports of goods or services or both, and inter-State supplies of persons having the same Permanent Account Number, computed on an all-India basis but excluding CGST, SGST, UTGST, IGST, and cess.
questions.notes: Definition question; answer is in cgst_act chunk covering definitions section.

questions.question: Who is liable for registration under the CGST Act?
questions.ground_truth: Every supplier whose aggregate turnover in a financial year exceeds the threshold limit (as notified) is liable to be registered under the CGST Act. Additionally, certain persons such as casual taxable persons, non-resident taxable persons, and those required to pay tax under reverse charge are compulsorily required to register.
questions.notes: Tests retrieval of the registration chapter; model must locate Section 22/24.

questions.question: What are the conditions a registered person must satisfy to claim Input Tax Credit (ITC) under the CGST Act?
questions.ground_truth: A registered person is entitled to ITC only if: (a) they possess a valid tax invoice or debit note from a registered supplier; (aa) the invoice details are furnished in the statement of outward supplies; (b) they have received the goods or services; (c) the tax charged has actually been paid to the government by the supplier; and (d) they have furnished a return.
questions.notes: Multi-condition compliance question requiring exact retrieval of Section 16 conditions.

questions.question: What is a 'composite supply' under the CGST Act and how is it taxed?
questions.ground_truth: A composite supply is a supply made by a taxable person to a recipient consisting of two or more taxable supplies of goods or services, naturally bundled in the ordinary course of business, one of which is the principal supply. A composite supply is taxed at the rate applicable to the principal supply.
questions.notes: Definition + rule question; chunk cgst_act_15 contains this definition.

questions.question: What are the penalties for committing fraud or wilful misstatement under the CGST Act?
questions.ground_truth: Under Section 74 of the CGST Act, where tax has not been paid or short paid due to fraud or wilful misstatement or suppression of facts, the proper officer may issue a notice and the person is liable to pay the tax along with interest and a penalty equal to the tax amount. Additionally, Section 122 prescribes penalties for specific offences.
questions.notes: Requires retrieval of fraud/penalty provisions; tests whether model can combine sections 74 and 122.

questions.question: What is the validity period of registration for a casual taxable person under the CGST Act?
questions.ground_truth: The certificate of registration issued to a casual taxable person is valid for the period specified in the application for registration or ninety days from the effective date of registration, whichever is earlier.
questions.notes: Specific factual detail from Section 27; chunk cgst_act_88 contains this.

questions.question: Under the CGST Act, is an agriculturist required to register for GST on the supply of agricultural produce?
questions.ground_truth: No. An agriculturist, to the extent of supply of produce out of cultivation of land, is not liable to be registered under the CGST Act.
questions.notes: Direct factual; answer is in the exemption provisions in cgst_act_80.

questions.question: What is the GST rate applicable to export of goods from India?
questions.ground_truth: The knowledge base (CGST Act text) does not specify individual GST rates for exports in the retrieved chunks, but exports of goods are treated as zero-rated supplies under the GST framework.
questions.notes: Rate schedules are not in the CGST Act text chunks. Model should say rates are not in the document rather than inventing specific percentages.

questions.question: Who is defined as a 'consumer' under the Consumer Protection Act, 2019?
questions.ground_truth: A consumer is any person who buys goods for consideration (not for resale or commercial purpose) or hires/avails of any service for consideration. It includes the user of goods or beneficiary of services other than the buyer, provided such use is with the approval of the buyer.
questions.notes: Fundamental definition question from the Consumer Protection Act definitions section.

questions.question: What are the six consumer rights recognised under the Consumer Protection Act, 2019?
questions.ground_truth: The six consumer rights include: (i) right to be protected from hazardous goods and services; (ii) right to be informed about quality, quantity, potency, purity, standard and price; (iii) right to access variety of goods at competitive prices; (iv) right to be heard; (v) right to seek redressal against unfair trade practices; (vi) right to consumer awareness/education.
questions.notes: Requires retrieval of Section 2(9); chunk consumer_act_10 contains the rights list.

questions.question: What constitutes an 'unfair trade practice' under the Consumer Protection Act, 2019?
questions.ground_truth: Unfair trade practice includes practices such as falsely representing goods as new when they are old/rebuilt, making false claims about quality or grade, false representation of sponsorship or approval, misleading representation about need for goods or services, and giving false facts about price.
questions.notes: chunk consumer_act_20 details specific unfair trade practice categories.

questions.question: How can a consumer file a complaint under the Consumer Protection Act, 2019, and where should it be filed?
questions.ground_truth: A complaint can be filed before the District Consumer Disputes Redressal Commission having jurisdiction where the opposite party resides or carries on business, or where the branch office is located, or where the cause of action arose, or where the complainant resides or personally works for gain.
questions.notes: Tests retrieval of jurisdiction provisions; chunk consumer_act_60 covers this.

questions.question: What is product liability under the Consumer Protection Act, 2019?
questions.ground_truth: Product liability refers to the responsibility of a product manufacturer, product service provider, or product seller for compensation to a consumer for any harm caused by a defective product. The Consumer Protection Act, 2019 includes a dedicated chapter on product liability.
questions.notes: Requires retrieval of Chapter VI product liability; chunk consumer_act_3 references it.

questions.question: What compensation can a consumer receive under the Consumer Protection Act if they suffer loss due to a defective product?
questions.ground_truth: The Consumer Protection Act, 2019 provides for product liability actions where a consumer can claim compensation for harm caused by a defective product from the product manufacturer, product service provider, or product seller. The specific quantum of compensation is determined by the Commission.
questions.notes: Tests combination of product liability and redressal provisions.

questions.question: What is the purpose of the Information Technology Act, 2000?
questions.ground_truth: The Information Technology Act, 2000 was enacted to provide legal recognition for transactions carried out by means of electronic data interchange and other means of electronic communication (electronic commerce), to facilitate electronic filing of documents with Government agencies, and to amend the Indian Penal Code and other related acts.
questions.notes: Direct purpose statement from the preamble; chunk it_act_5 contains this.

questions.question: What is the penalty for unauthorised access to a computer system under the IT Act, 2000?
questions.ground_truth: Under Section 43 of the IT Act, if any person without permission accesses or secures access to a computer, computer system or computer network, they shall be liable to pay damages by way of compensation to the person affected. Section 66 provides for imprisonment up to 3 years and/or fine up to 5 lakh rupees for computer-related offences.
questions.notes: Penalty question requiring retrieval of Section 43; chunk it_act_43 is key.

questions.question: What is a 'protected system' under the IT Act, 2000, and what are the consequences of unauthorised access to it?
questions.ground_truth: A protected system is any computer resource declared by the appropriate Government by notification in the Official Gazette that directly or indirectly affects the facility of Critical Information Infrastructure. Unauthorised access to a protected system is an offence under the IT Act.
questions.notes: Specific technical-legal question from Section 70; chunk it_act_70 contains this.

questions.question: Under the IT Act, 2000, can a company be held liable for a cyber offence committed by one of its employees?
questions.ground_truth: Yes. Under Section 85 of the IT Act, if a contravention of any provision is committed by a company, every person who at the time of the contravention was in charge of and responsible for the conduct of business shall be guilty of the contravention. However, no liability attaches if the person proves the contravention occurred without their knowledge or that they exercised due diligence.
questions.notes: Corporate liability provision in Section 85; chunk it_act_85 contains this.

questions.question: What is the meaning of 'cyber security' as defined in the IT Act, 2000?
questions.ground_truth: Cyber security means protecting information, equipment, devices, computers, computer resources, communication devices and information stored therein from unauthorised access, use, disclosure, disruption, modification or destruction.
questions.notes: Definitional question; chunk it_act_10 contains the definition.

questions.question: What is the Essential Commodities Act, 1955, and what is its purpose?
questions.ground_truth: The Essential Commodities Act, 1955 (Act No. 10 of 1955) is an Act to provide, in the interest of the general public, for the control of the production, supply and distribution of, and trade and commerce in, certain essential commodities. It came into force on 1st April 1955.
questions.notes: Direct purpose statement from the Act's preamble; chunk essential_commodities_1.

questions.question: What powers does the Central Government have to control the supply and distribution of essential commodities?
questions.ground_truth: Under Section 3 of the Essential Commodities Act, the Central Government may control production, supply, distribution and trade of essential commodities by issuing orders for licensing, permits, fixing prices, and regulation of stocks if it considers it necessary for maintaining supplies or securing equitable distribution.
questions.notes: Tests retrieval of Section 3 powers; chunk essential_commodities_5 is key.

questions.question: What is the punishment for violating an order issued under the Essential Commodities Act, 1955?
questions.ground_truth: Under the Essential Commodities Act, a person who contravenes an order made under Section 3 shall be punishable with imprisonment for a term not less than six months but which may extend to seven years, and shall also be liable to a fine. The court may, for adequate and special reasons, impose a sentence of less than six months.
questions.notes: Penalty provision in chunk essential_commodities_35.

questions.question: Can a company be held liable for an offence committed under the Essential Commodities Act?
questions.ground_truth: Yes. Under the Essential Commodities Act, if an offence is committed by a company and it is proved that the offence occurred with the consent or connivance of, or is attributable to neglect by, any director, manager, secretary or other officer of the company, that officer shall also be deemed guilty and liable to be punished.
questions.notes: Corporate liability provision; chunk essential_commodities_40 covers this.

questions.question: What is the income tax slab rate for individuals earning between 5 lakh and 10 lakh rupees per year in India?
questions.ground_truth: This information is not available in the PolicyCheck knowledge base. The knowledge base contains the CGST Act, Consumer Protection Act, IT Act, and Essential Commodities Act. Income tax slabs are defined in the Income Tax Act, which is not part of the current knowledge base.
questions.notes: Hallucination trap: income tax rates are NOT in the KB. The correct response is to say the information was not found in the policy documents.
